To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the rice mutant γ278 was identified with increased RS content.

the rice mutant with increased resistant starch was developed by utilizing γ-rays as a mutagen and the mutant was characterized for mutations/variants in starch biosynthetic gene viz., GBSSI (GBSSI:G1138C, G1150A, G1173C), SSI (SSI:C1182T), SSIIa (SSIIa:G1159A, A1161G), SSIIIa (SSIIIa:G1139T, C1161A)
the rice mutant γ278 was characterized by the mutations in the starch genes GBSSI, SBEIIb, SSI, SSIa, and SIIIa, and the combination of GBSSI:ssIIa:sIIIa is responsible for high RS in rice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a high RS rice mutant, identification of the genes responsible for high RS, and the development of molecular marker combinations to develop a high RS rice variety.
the identification of functional mutations/variants in starch biosynthetic pathway genes in rice mutant γ278 and its effect on RS content.
the development of rice variety with increased dietary fibre content and its characterization at molecular level.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the study has identified three deleterious mutations in GBSSI, SIIa, and SIIIa genes that are responsible for high RS in mutant γ278.
this study has identified a marker combination that can be used to develop high RS rice variety.
the present work has identified a set of SNPs (GBSSI, ssIIa, and ssIIIa) that can be used as markers to develop a rice cultivar with high RS content.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this study is the first report to identify the functional mutations/variants in GBSSI, SBEIb, SSIIa and SSIIIa that led to high RS in rice.
the combination of GBSSI:ssIIa: ssIIIa SNP is responsible for high RS in rice mutant γ278.
the combination of deleterous mutation/variant (GBSSI:ssIIIa:ssIIa) can be used to improve the quality of rice by increasing RS content.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the high RS rice mutant γ278 can be utilized as a donor for developing high RS rice varieties with high amylose and RS content.
we have identified the functional SNPs in the starch biosynthesis genes which will be useful in developing a rice mutant with high RS.
the SNP combinations in the starch biosynthesis genes can be used to increase RS content and hence, the nutritional quality of rice.
